prose_updates.tldr: A finite observed law is lifted to one joint law of treatment and both potential outcomes, and the least Pearson assignment information needed to support each ATE is profiled. The attained sharp frontier has a perspective SOCP and explicit dual. For binary outcomes, a treatment-independent garbling removes the minority discordant response type without imposing monotone treatment response and without increasing any convex assignment cost; this yields the complete six-face scalar catalog and a squared-correlation null identity. A one-way, cost-nonincreasing embedding into the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14) gives the exact separation \(9/70>9/91\). With neighborhood radius at most \(1/10\), explicit positive mass, support, arm-variance, and treatment-variance bounds make continuity preserve a uniformly positive gap on a positive-volume open neighborhood. On the named uniformly Slater-regular multinomial region, the observed-cell floor itself gives \(e_x\) and \(1-e_x\) at least \(K\delta\) for every profiled law; a fixed-odds-cone parametrization, uniform equality right inverse, and bounded attained cellwise dual multipliers then yield a finite-sample \(O(n^{-1/2})\) profile diameter without transporting a dual certificate between laws. A contiguous boundary pair shows that honest bands must retain infinite diameter at a finite-to-infinite null-cost boundary.

project_justification.gap: Average-case sensitivity analysis has sharp armwise potential-outcome bounds but no jointly attained ATE frontier. Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's equations~(10), (12), and (14) provide an observed-policy-first divergence and Jensen--CMC computation, but they do not establish that their armwise weights are generated by one cross-world-compatible assignment law. The present comparison therefore requires a one-way full-law embedding into a separately defined box-augmented Neyman specialization on the same budget scale; it neither identifies nor strictly tightens the unqualified published class. Existing inference theory also does not quantify both the regular finite-sample width and the finite-to-infinite boundary obstruction for this frontier.
project_justification.niche: Finite outcomes make the missing joint law explicit, expose a response-type garbling geometry invisible to armwise reweighting, and permit an interior finite-dimensional comparison. Explicit neighborhood bounds show that the rational comparison is robust on a positive-volume set rather than a knife-edge witness.
project_justification.fill: The project profiles the exact full-law Pearson cost, certifies it by primal and dual conic programs, solves the binary geometry, and maps every compatible full law one way into the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14) at no greater cost. It proves the exact values \(9/70\) and \(9/91\), then uses a radius no larger than \(1/10\), strictly interior scalar optimizers, and explicit positive support and variance bounds to obtain a uniform positive gap on a nonempty open neighborhood. It also pairs a finite-sample regular-region diameter theorem, whose cross-law overlap is derived directly from the observed-cell floor, with a contiguous boundary lower bound.

prose_updates.related_work: Zhang and Zhao motivate average rather than worst-case assignment distortion and prove sharp bounds for each average potential outcome, but their discussion explicitly withholds joint ATE attainment. Ishikawa, He, and Kanamori define an observed-policy-first \(f\)-divergence in equation~(10), apply Jensen in equation~(12), and combine the relaxed divergence with CMC in equation~(14). The comparison here is deliberately one way: every compatible full law induces a feasible point of the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization with no larger cost. No equality with, strict tightening of, or reverse realizability for their unqualified published class is claimed. The rational witness has values \(9/70\) and \(9/91\); after restricting the coordinate radius to at most \(1/10\), explicit positive lower bounds for neighborhood mass, observable support, arm variance, and treatment variance make the strictly positive gap uniform on a positive-volume open neighborhood. Balke and Pearl supply the finite response-type representation, and Manski supplies the substantive monotone-response benchmark; the binary garbling result instead derives monotone support for an extremal compatible law without assuming monotone treatment response of the population. The regular finite-sample theorem rescales response-type masses onto a common odds cone. For every profiled law, its observed-cell floor yields \(e_x\geq K\delta\) and \(1-e_x\geq K\delta\); the proof then derives a uniform right inverse and multiplier bound and compares laws through each law's own saddle identity. Duan, Zhang, and Zhang derive directional derivatives for finite-valued Slater-regular SOCP values, while Fang and Santos and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker supply derivative-aware statistical inference; extending those tools through zero perspective cells and moving faces remains the open tangent-inference question.
prose_updates.interpretation: For computation across a finite covariate alphabet, additivity of the ATE and Pearson cost permits the observation \(C_P(t)=\min\{\sum_x p_x C_x(t_x):\sum_xp_xt_x=t\}\), with conditional minimizers glued stratum by stratum into a compatible full law. This is used as a computational decomposition, not retained as a numbered proposition. Substantively, the frontier reports the least assignment information required by a jointly compatible potential-outcome law; the note-defined Jensen--CMC value is a one-way lower-cost screen and not a certificate of reverse cross-world realizability.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The interior binary stationarity equation is generically quintic, so the exact catalog isolates a unique algebraic root and does not promise universal radical formulas. The regular-profile constant depends on the fixed-cone interior radius and the smallest singular value of the equality operator. Its cross-law coefficient bounds use the explicit regular-region overlap \(\kappa_\delta=K\delta\), derived from the observed-cell floor, and can deteriorate as \(\delta\) approaches zero. The boundary lower bound shows that this deterioration reflects a genuine statistical discontinuity at the null-feasibility boundary.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The sharpness, dual attainment, garbling, scalar catalog, one-way cost transfer into the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization, exact rational separation, positive-volume open-neighborhood uniform gap, regular-region finite-sample diameter, and boundary impossibility are theorem claims proved in the note. The comparison does not identify that specialization with Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's unqualified published class, does not claim a strict tightening of that class, and does not assert that every relaxed armwise weight is induced by a compatible cross-world assignment law. The local comparison uses radius at most \(1/10\) and records explicit positive lower bounds for neighborhood mass and observable support, arm variance, and treatment variance. The regular diameter proof derives cross-law overlap from the regular-region cell floor and controls coefficient movement through a common fixed odds cone and a law-specific saddle comparison; it does not claim active-set stability or feasibility of one law's dual certificate at another law. The finite-stratum infimal-convolution identity is retained only as a computational observation. Uniform tangent inference through zero perspective cells, optimizer ties, and moving odds faces remains open. The \(\Gamma=1\) specialization is retained only as a regression corollary. The application target remains a prespecified categorical mercury score and finite covariate stratification; it does not claim to recover the original continuous-outcome NHANES estimand.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem converts multinomial concentration into an honest finite-sample simultaneous band with \(O(n^{-1/2})\) diameter. For every profiled law in the named regular region, summing the positive cells in each treatment arm gives the explicit cross-law bounds \(e_x\geq K\delta\) and \(1-e_x\geq K\delta\); these bounds support the common-cone scaling, coefficient estimates, equality right inverse, and attained-multiplier bound.
statement_notes.gap: ZhangZhao2026AverageCase gives regular bands for armwise sensitivity curves; it does not control the finite-sample diameter of a jointly compatible ATE cost frontier through an observed-cell-derived cross-law overlap bound, a uniform fixed-cone Slater radius, and a law-specific saddle comparison.
statement_notes.consumer: The categorical-mercury analysis obtains a finite-width simultaneous frontier band whenever its prespecified cells and ATE range satisfy the reported observed-cell, cone-slack, and equality-rank margins; it need not assume that the true-law overlap constant automatically applies to every profiled multinomial law.

statement_notes.justification: The inverse-propensity construction proves only a one-way, cost-nonincreasing map from compatible full laws into the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14), while the exact rational witness quantifies the additional cost imposed by one cross-world-compatible assignment mechanism.
statement_notes.gap: IshikawaHeKanamori2026Convex supplies the observed-policy-first divergence, Jensen step, and CMC architecture, but does not prove reverse cross-world realizability or the \(9/70\) versus \(9/91\) comparison for the note-defined specialization. No strict tightening of the unqualified published class is asserted.
statement_notes.consumer: A sensitivity analyst may use the note-defined specialization as a one-way lower-cost screen, but cannot infer that its feasible weights are generated by a compatible full law.

statement_notes.justification: After choosing the neighborhood radius no larger than \(1/10\), the proof records positive lower bounds \( (1/2-\eta)(1/5-\eta)\) for the smallest observable cell, \( (1/5-\eta)(4/5-\eta)\) for each arm's outcome variance, and \( (1/2-\eta)^2\) for treatment variance. Strictly interior minimizers and continuity then preserve a uniform positive cost gap on a positive-volume parameter neighborhood.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem rules out a knife-edge explanation for the rational witness while remaining a comparison only with the note-defined box-augmented specialization, not with an unqualified published feasible class.
statement_notes.consumer: Small multinomial perturbations of the treated fraction and arm success probabilities preserve both well-defined scalar programs and a uniformly positive separation.
